purpose: Assign exactly one primary scientific full-text exclusion reason to a retrieved report that is demonstrably ineligible for the peer-reviewed core A/B map. Preserve other failed dimensions in reviewer notes.

primary_reason_rule.instruction: Choose the first established reason in this hierarchy. Do not code an unresolved or merely unreported fact as an exclusion. If a reason is uncertain, use awaiting classification. A report may have secondary failed dimensions in notes, but only one primary full-text code.

codes.label: Source type is not eligible for peer-reviewed core map
codes.definition: Review, editorial, protocol, or conference abstract without an eligible full paper. Public preprints are routed to the separate frontier register, not assigned a core full-text exclusion code; if a peer-reviewed version exists, screen that version and link/deduplicate reports.
examples: Narrative or systematic review
Study protocol without results
Conference abstract only

codes.label: No eligible original human research
codes.definition: Animal-only, in-vitro-only, computational-only without eligible original human measurements, or other non-human report.
examples: Rodent exercise experiment only
Cell culture stimulation without human participant data

codes.label: Population outside target (under 18 y, clinical/infected) or eligible adult healthy stratum not separable
codes.definition: Participants are children or adolescents (< 18 y) as stated in the report; or a mixed-age cohort that the report states includes participants < 18 y has no separable adult (>= 18 y) stratum with results; or participants have active infection or known clinical/metabolic disease, or are a disease-treatment/clinical cohort outside the generally healthy target; or a mixed cohort's eligible generally healthy stratum and results cannot be separated. Older adults are eligible and are flagged as a subgroup, not excluded. Metabolic-health ambiguity alone is not sufficient; adjudicate explicitly using reported diagnoses and stratum separability. Age rule (v3.1, PRE-004): a cohort, or each separately reported group, is adult when an explicit age range or minimum age >= 18 y is reported, or mean - 2*SD >= 18 y (SD as reported; SEM, IQR or descriptors such as "adults", "students" do not substitute). Otherwise the record is AWAITING_CLASSIFICATION, not FT03, unless the report states that participants < 18 y were included. An unreported age, or a mean - 2*SD below 18 y without a stated range or minimum, therefore remains awaiting classification, not FT03.
examples: Adolescent-only cohort (for example 13-17 y)
Mixed adolescent/adult cohort reporting pooled results only
Exercise intervention in a disease-treatment cohort
Active infection cohort
Mixed healthy and clinical sample with no separable eligible results
NOT FT03: age reported only as mean 20.9 (SD 1.8) y (mean - 2*SD = 17.3 y) with no stated range or minimum -> AWAITING_CLASSIFICATION

codes.label: No identifiable acute bout or qualifying repeated-bout monitoring
codes.definition: Neither an identifiable acute bout/competition for Core A nor Support B's same immune-related marker measured after at least two identified bouts in the same participants with known or reliably recoverable sample-to-bout relations is present. Any identifiable bout qualifies regardless of intensity, duration or mode: these are recorded at extraction and are never eligibility thresholds, so a low-intensity or short bout is not FT04. Support B is retained as the cross-bout open-window monitoring layer. Establish the exposure failure from the source; unknown timing remains awaiting classification. Evaluate post-cessation sampling and baseline/comparator separately under FT05 and FT06. v3.1: when such a report is otherwise an original, generally healthy adult human study with an eligible immune link and fails only through a background pattern (habitual/resting cross-sectional comparison, periodic or seasonal monitoring with unknown last-bout timing, training snapshot with unknown exercise-to-sampling interval), the full-text disposition is RETAIN_BACKGROUND (administrative; FT04 recorded as a secondary failed dimension), not EXCLUDE_FT.
examples: Habitual exercise versus sedentary cross-sectional comparison only
General seasonal or weekly sampling with unknown relation to exercise bouts
Training pre/post comparison with no recoverable acute bout or post-exercise sampling relation

codes.label: No sample collected after exercise cessation
codes.definition: For an otherwise qualifying acute exercise report, immune sampling occurs only during exercise and there is no post-cessation sample. This code does not apply when a post-cessation sample exists but is immediate (<30 minutes).
examples: During-only sampling with no sample after cessation

codes.label: No pre-bout baseline or suitable non-exercise/comparator condition
codes.definition: The report has no pre-bout baseline and no suitable non-exercise/comparator condition enabling interpretation of an otherwise qualifying post-exercise immune measure. For B, the required baseline/comparator is absent.
examples: Post-exercise sample only, with no baseline or comparator in report or linked report

codes.label: No eligible immune measure or immune-focused omics analysis
codes.definition: No direct immune-cell/count/subset/function measure, recognized immune mediator, immune-cell omics, or biofluid omics with a stated immune objective/analysis and identifiable immune candidates is present.
examples: Cortisol-only response
CK, lactate, or HRV only
General muscle/metabolic omics with merely post-hoc immune pathway enrichment and no stated immune objective/analysis

codes.label: Exercise effect inseparable from a mixed intervention
codes.definition: Exercise is combined with feeding, supplementation, or another intervention and the study design provides no interpretable control/placebo or factorial contrast separating the exercise effect relevant to this review. A placebo label alone is insufficient; an interpretable exercise contrast or pre-bout baseline in the unaffected arm must be established.
examples: All participants receive exercise and an active supplement with no comparator or separable contrast

not_scientific_exclusion_statuses.meaning: Duplicate bibliographic record identified during deduplication.
not_scientific_exclusion_statuses.handling: Retain provenance, duplicate-to-retained linkage and rationale; count administratively outside scientific exclusion reasons.

not_scientific_exclusion_statuses.meaning: Superseded version of the same report, such as a preprint with a linked peer-reviewed publication.
not_scientific_exclusion_statuses.handling: Link to the retained publication/version, retain version metadata and do not double count. Distinct complementary reports from one cohort remain linked rather than discarded.

not_scientific_exclusion_statuses.meaning: Full text remains unavailable after institutional access attempts.
not_scientific_exclusion_statuses.handling: Awaiting classification; keep outside scientific full-text exclusion counts; no full-text exclusion code.

not_scientific_exclusion_statuses.meaning: A report in a language other than directly read English or Chinese is awaiting translation and independent human checking.
not_scientific_exclusion_statuses.handling: No language-based exclusion; keep outside scientific full-text exclusion counts.

not_scientific_exclusion_statuses.meaning: A material fact such as timing, health status, cohort linkage, or intervention separability is unresolved.
not_scientific_exclusion_statuses.handling: Keep pending and resolve from full text/supplement or adjudication; do not infer failure.

not_scientific_exclusion_statuses.meaning: Public preprint with no peer-reviewed version at the final update.
not_scientific_exclusion_statuses.handling: Track in the separate frontier register; do not count as core evidence or as a scientific full-text exclusion.

not_scientific_exclusion_statuses.meaning: Full-text disposition (v3.1, PRE-004) for a retrieved, original, generally healthy adult human study with an eligible immune link whose only failure is exposure/timing in a background pattern: habitual-exercise or resting cross-sectional comparison; periodic, weekly or seasonal monitoring with unknown last-bout timing; or training pre/post snapshot with unknown exercise-to-sampling interval.
not_scientific_exclusion_statuses.handling: Administrative, not a scientific exclusion: no primary FT code (the failed dimension, normally FT04, goes to secondary_failed_dimensions); maps to scope_stream background; charted at reduced depth (bibliographic, design, population, platforms and n; one extractor plus one checker) in the background register; outside every original-study denominator and shown as its own line in the PRISMA flow. Full-text stage only; not a census of background literature. Reviews, animal/in-vitro reports and post-hoc-pathway-only reports keep their FT code (EXCLUDE_FT).

explicitly_not_exclusion_reasons: No functional assay or functional evidence
No individualized baseline, personalized model, or precision terminology
No clinical prediction or external validation
Immediate post-cessation sample collected before 30 minutes

Sampling later than 72 hours, including studies whose only post-cessation samples are later than 72 hours, when the relation to the identifiable bout remains identifiable (samples are tagged outside-window recovery)
Inaccessible full text before institutional access attempts are documented
Small sample size alone, including otherwise eligible generally healthy case observations/series
Low exercise intensity, short duration or any particular exercise mode (recorded; no exposure threshold)
No use of the term 'open window' or any author stance on it (endorsing, rejecting or omitting the hypothesis)
Older-adult cohort (included and flagged as a subgroup)
window_and_exposure_note: v3 contract 2.1-2.2: there is no exposure-intensity threshold, and 0-72 h after cessation is an organising window, not an inclusion cap. Samples later than 72 h are extracted and tagged outside-window recovery. No exclusion code or administrative status refers to the window; FT05 applies only to during-only sampling. v3.1 (PRE-004) adds one administrative status, RETAIN_BACKGROUND, for background reports; the FT01-FT08 hierarchy is unchanged. v3.1 (PRE-005) adds a title-only screening stage whose closed list of title-evident reasons maps onto FT01-FT04 and FT07 (title_stage_closed_list); FT01-FT08 are unchanged.
title_abstract_reason_rule: At title/abstract, EXCLUDE_TA records one primary_reason drawn from the same FT01-FT08 codes, naming the first clearly failed dimension in hierarchy order. There are no separate TA reason codes. Criteria that can only be judged in full text are not TA exclusion grounds.

title_stage_closed_list.stage: TI (stage 1: title screening; reviewers see title, source/journal, year, document type, DOI and PMID only; no abstract and no AI hint)
title_stage_closed_list.purpose: Closed list of the only reasons for which a record may be excluded at title screening (disposition EXCLUDE_TITLE). Each reason must be evident from the title or the exported document type; each maps to one FT code so that title-stage exclusions can be reported in the FT hierarchy. Anything not covered, or not evident, is ADVANCE_TO_ABSTRACT.
title_stage_closed_list.primary_reason_rule: EXCLUDE_TITLE records exactly one closed-list code: the first evident reason in the order below, which follows the FT hierarchy. If no listed reason is evident, the decision is ADVANCE_TO_ABSTRACT; if the title cannot be read or the record identity is unclear, AWAITING_CLASSIFICATION. Doubt never excludes.
title_stage_closed_list.not_title_stage_reasons: FT05, FT06 and FT08; clinical, diseased or infected cohorts; health status; timing relative to the bout; comparator; mixed interventions; preprint status; language; missing abstract; and every item of explicitly_not_exclusion_reasons. These are judged at stage 2 or at full text.

codes.label: Review, editorial, protocol or conference abstract evident from the title or document type
evident_when: The exported document type is Review, Systematic Review, Meta-Analysis, Editorial, Editorial Material, Comment, Meeting Abstract or Conference Abstract, and no source exports the record as an original article
The title states that the report is a review (narrative, systematic, scoping or umbrella), meta-analysis, position stand, consensus statement, editorial or commentary
The title states a study or trial protocol, or "design and rationale", without results
not_sufficient: Letter, research letter, correspondence, short communication, case report, or full conference/proceedings paper (may contain original data)
Words such as overview, update, perspective or insights in a title exported as an original article
Document types that disagree across sources, unless the title itself states the source type

codes.label: Animal-only or in-vitro-only study evident from the title
evident_when: The title names only non-human organisms (for example mice, rats, murine, rodent, equine, horses, dogs, pigs, zebrafish)
The title describes only cell lines or cultured cells, with no human participants
not_sufficient: Humans and animals both named, or the organism not named
Ex vivo or in vitro assays on samples from human participants (for example stimulated human blood)
Computational or secondary analyses of human data (not on the closed list; judged at stage 2)

codes.label: Cohort clearly under 18 years in the title
evident_when: The title names only participants under 18 years: children, adolescents, adolescent athletes, schoolchildren, boys or girls, infants, paediatric/pediatric, an age range entirely below 18 years, or an under-18 age-group team (for example U-16)
not_sufficient: Mixed adolescent and adult groups (for example "adolescent and adult athletes")
young, young adults, youth, junior, students, college or collegiate, cadets, recruits, or no age descriptor
Clinical, diseased or infected cohorts (not on the closed list; judged at stage 2 under FT03)

codes.label: No exercise or physical-activity context evident in the title
evident_when: The title describes the study exposure or topic, that exposure is evidently not exercise or physical activity (for example a drug, diet-only, vaccine, sleep, surgery, disease course or psychological-stress study), and the title contains no reference to exercise, physical activity, sport, training, athletes, competition, physical exertion or a physically demanding occupational or military task
not_sufficient: A title that names no exposure at all (for example only markers, cells or a population): the exercise context may be in the abstract
Fitness, VO2max, sedentary behaviour, steps, physical work or any form of training named in the title
Habitual or cross-sectional physical activity (judged at stage 2 or full text; possible RETAIN_BACKGROUND)

codes.label: No immune, inflammatory or omics content evident in the title
evident_when: The title names the study outcomes and none is immune, inflammatory or omics content (for example only performance, VO2max, strength, glycogen, lactate, heart-rate variability, cortisol or other hormones, bone, cognition or mood)
not_sufficient: A title that names no outcome

Generic or possibly immune content: blood or salivary markers, biomarkers, recovery or stress markers, proteins, plasma, serum, saliva, gene expression, muscle damage, oxidative stress, infection, illness, upper respiratory symptoms or health
Any immune cell, cytokine, immunoglobulin, complement, inflammation, leukocyte or omics term

title_stage_closed_list.conflict_rule: Title-stage consensus is automatic: any ADVANCE_TO_ABSTRACT by either reviewer wins; EXCLUDE_TITLE is final only when both reviewers chose it (if their codes differ, the earlier code in this list is recorded and the difference logged); every other combination is AWAITING_CLASSIFICATION, which proceeds to stage 2 with the advanced records. Conflicts are logged, not adjudicated.
title_stage_closed_list.reporting: PRISMA-ScR flow: title-stage exclusions are reported as a separate box, by closed-list code and its FT code.
